title: Getting a big tone and reed strength
summary: He says players use too soft a reed; he uses a number three.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: I know, that's hard to describe. I know that. I was wondering about your tone. You have not only a beautiful tone, but one of the good, full, big tones, which a lot of players, especially the younger players, now don't get a big tone. They're always covered up by the brass, the trumpet and trombone, which they can't cover you up. I wonder, how do you get that big tone? You don't look like you're blowing extra hard.
Is it something about peace? I think the main trouble is that they use too soft a reed.
How hard a reed do you use? I use three.
